A private design charrette · four engines, one house

51 Trichard Street
four ways to make it modern

The same brief, with the same seven photographs, put to Codex, Claude, Qwen and Hermes. Each had to commit to a single direction and price it. They agree on more than you would expect, and split cleanly on one thing: the thatch.

51 Carl Trichard St, Ohrigstad, 1122 · Limpopo Open in Google Maps ↗ −24.7453939, 30.5653748 11 November 2026

The subject

A modern shell wearing three costumes

Underneath the finishes there is a competent house: a strong cantilevered upper slab, glass that opens the living floor to the sky, a courtyard, a pool, and a boundary wall that is the only real piece of architecture on the street. What all four engines independently called out is the finish confusion — brown stacked stone, grey metal siding, fake-timber garage doors, a thatch cone at the back and turquoise water, none of them agreeing.

The house sits on the Lowveld escarpment edge: 30–35°C wet summers with violent afternoon thunderstorms, dry high-UV winters, dust, and borers that will eat any exposed timber given a season. Every engine was briefed on that climate and told not to specify timber where it cannot survive.

The four

Where they land

01 Lowveld Shade House Codex 02 Termitarium House Claude 03 Modern Kraal Qwen 04 One Wall, One Roof Hermes

Unanimous, four out of four

The property wears too many competing materials and one of them has to go.

All masonry — wall, house, lapa piers — gets one continuous skin, so the house and its wall read as a single object rather than a house hiding behind a barricade.

Every timber and timber-look element is replaced with powder-coated aluminium or steel. Nothing a borer can eat stays on the outside.

The wall keeps its height. Nobody proposed lowering it; security was not on the table.

The split: three to one

Claude keeps the thatch. Reed on brick is the Lowveld’s own answer to heat; re-comb it, treat it with an approved fire retardant, put a lightning mast on it, replace borer-eaten poles.

Codex, Qwen and Hermes all remove it, for the same three reasons: it is a second roof language fighting the flat roof, it cannot stop driven rain, and it is a borer and insurance liability.

Budget runs R 950 000 to R 1 900 000 across the four; timeline 12 to 14 weeks of construction, after approvals.

01
Codex

Lowveld Shade House

OpenAI · gpt-6.1-sol via codex-cli 0.167.1

The engineer’s answer: shade, drainage, metal that cannot rot.

Grounded Sheltered Resolute
I would make this house quieter, heavier and more deeply shaded. Keep its substantial walls, familiar rooms and pool; give them one pale mineral skin and a bronze aluminium veil. Replace the thatch with a thin insulated pavilion roof. Spend on shade, drainage and durable finishes. The result should feel unmistakably Lowveld: sheltered from violent weather, open to courtyard life, and warm without depending on timber.

Thesis Turn the existing house into a pale mineral courtyard retreat, unified by bronze metalwork and deep, inhabitable shade.

Palette

Warm Limestone #D8CEB8 Fine mineral render across retained street masonry, house masonry and lapa piers.
Dry Bronze #655747 Solid-colour aluminium balcony fins, both gates and replacement garage doors; no timber imitation.
Pale Chalk #EEE9DD Upper siding, wide fascia, carport edge and new pavilion roof; light surfaces limit solar heat gain.
River Sand #C5B391 Textured porcelain pool paving and matching rounded coping.
Bush Olive #687158 Retained hedges, indigenous planting and replaceable outdoor cushions.

What changes, surface by surface

Street edge · wall, gates, the 51

Keep the wall's height, brick piers and security line. Remove pyramidal pier caps; introduce simple precast caps with drips. Prepare the face brick with a bonded render system and finish in warm limestone mineral coating, retaining movement joints. Replace the scrollwork pedestrian gate and vehicle gate leaf with matching vertical aluminium fins over hot-dip-galvanised steel frames, superdurable polyester powder-coated bronze. Preserve sliding operation; reassess motor capacity for the new leaf. Consolidate intercom and letterbox in one flush bronze panel with a large cut-out, softly backlit 51. Keep the tall hedge; introduce indigenous grasses inside the boundary to soften the courtyard without obstructing street sightlines.

Facade · stone, siding, garage doors

Keep both storeys, existing openings, glazing and flat-roof silhouette. Remove applied stacked-stone veneer only; the photographs also show substantial brickwork, which stays. Repair exposed substrates and render house masonry in the same limestone finish as the wall. Retain sound horizontal metal siding and fascia, prepared and recoated pale chalk using a substrate-compatible system. Replace both timber-look garage doors with plain bronze powder-coated aluminium sectional doors. Add an independently supported, open bronze aluminium fin screen along the balcony's outer edge, with a deep overhead shade blade and operable sections outside the sliding glazing. Retain a separately compliant balustrade behind it; fins do not substitute for fall protection. Inspect and repair balcony waterproofing before refinishing.

Lapa & pool

Replace the conical thatch and its timber structure, including the adjoining thatched veranda strip, with one visually thin, rectangular pavilion roof over the existing entertaining footprint. Use an engineered hot-dip-galvanised steel frame, pale factory-coated concealed-fix steel roofing at a proposed five-degree fall, mineral-wool insulation and a ventilated fibre-cement soffit. Keep sound masonry piers, foundations, built-in braai and dining furniture; render the piers limestone. Provide an engineered chimney transition, fire clearances and independently sized external gutters with visible overflow routes. Keep the pool shell and water colour. Lift the tan deck tiles; repair the base and lay sand-coloured porcelain certified for wet barefoot pool use, with rounded coping, movement joints and falls to accessible drains. Replace blue loungers with bronze aluminium frames and olive outdoor fabric. Retain the evergreen backdrop.

The signature

A room-deep bronze veil across the existing upper balcony: vertical aluminium fins cast long moving stripes over pale walls and paving, with one pivoting section opening toward the pool courtyard. This is the house's single defining gesture, made in metal that borers cannot consume. Final depth and fin angles follow measured solar orientation, wind loading and views.

Five moves, priced

01Quiet the boundary Render retained wall and piers; fit flat caps, matching aluminium gates, consolidated services and illuminated 51.R 180 000 to R 250 000
02Unify the existing house Strip applied veneer, repair substrates and balcony waterproofing, render masonry, recoat siding and fascia, and install two aluminium garage doors.R 280 000 to R 390 000
03Build the bronze veil Install engineered balcony shade frame, aluminium fins, overhead blade and operable panels; retain independent compliant guarding and protect waterproofing at fixings.R 150 000 to R 220 000
04Replace the thatch Remove both thatched roofs; erect insulated steel pavilion roofing with fibre-cement soffits, braai flue adaptation, gutters and stormwater connections.R 280 000 to R 380 000

Budget band R 1 350 000 to R 1 900 000 total; indicative 2026 installed allowances including VAT, Limpopo mobilisation, professional design and engineering fees, approvals and 15% construction contingency. Quantities remain unmeasured; allow approximately 65 square metres of pavilion roofing and 100 square metres of pool paving. Excludes interior refurbishment and pool-shell replacement.
Duration 12 weeks
Hardest risk

Hidden moisture damage and inadequate existing supports at the connected lapa/veranda roof could turn roof replacement into structural reconstruction. A professional must survey the roof junctions, foundations and drainage before pricing, then engineer the new frame and obtain approvals. Twelve weeks covers phased construction after approvals and procurement; keep a secure entrance and usable living zone throughout, and sequence roof removal within a planned dry-weather window.

02
Claude

Termitarium House

Anthropic · Claude Code 2.1.322, model ‘opus’

The biologist’s answer: copy the termite mound, keep the thatch.

monolithic earthen calm
Every house in the Lowveld loses its timber to insects. So stop fighting them and copy them. The termite mound is the best building in this landscape: one earth-red mass, thick, self-shading, with nothing in it for a borer to eat. 51 Trichard already has good bones, a solid face-brick house with a strong cantilevered slab, but it wears too many costumes: tan brick, grey boards, fake-timber doors and spear-topped gates. I take the costumes off and turn the whole property into one ochre mass, from the street wall to the lapa columns, under a dark oxide-metal lid. The thatch stays, because reed on brick is what this place invented. The wall stays high. It just stops scowling.

Thesis Turn the house's enemy into its model: one bagged, earth-red mass, capped in oxide metal, with no exposed timber anywhere.

Palette

Termitarium Ochre #B5683E Mineral-silicate limewash over bagged brick: street wall, piers, ground floor, upper brick piers, lapa columns, cracked retaining wall
Burnt Mound #4E2A20 Matte powder-coat and pre-painted steel: upper-box cladding, fascias, both gates, garage doors, balustrade, carport fascia
Lowveld Dust #D8B68C Soffits, window and door reveals, the lit reveal behind the 51, coloured screed at thresholds
Reed Straw #A58A5C The existing thatch, kept and re-combed; matched by the aggregate in the new pool coping
Mopane Pool #1F2C27 Charcoal-green marbelite pool interior, so the pool reads as a dark mirror instead of a blue rectangle

What changes, surface by surface

Street edge · wall, gates, the 51

The wall keeps its full height (security is not negotiable here) but stops reading as a barricade. All face brick is bagged and finished in one Termitarium Ochre mineral-silicate limewash; the white precast pier caps go, replaced by flat tops with a concealed Burnt Mound steel drip flashing. The spear-topped sliding gate and the steel palisade infill panels become flush vertical aluminium battens (50x25 mm, 15 mm gaps) in Burnt Mound on the existing motor and track. The pedestrian gate becomes a solid 2.4 m pivot door. The stainless numerals and postbox come off; 51 is cut through the new door (see signature) and the post slot is a flush steel letterbox set into the wall. The verge strip becomes aloes and spekboom, not lawn.

Facade · stone, siding, garage doors

The photographs show the ground floor in multi-tone face brick, not stacked stone; it is bagged and limewashed Termitarium Ochre together with the upper brick piers and the cracked white retaining wall by the stairs, so house and wall read as one carved mass. The mid-grey horizontal boards on the upper boxes are stripped and replaced with 0.55 mm AZ150 pre-painted steel standing seam laid vertically in Burnt Mound, with the wide fascia wrapped in the same sheet: a dark lid on an earth body. The maroon timber-look garage doors become insulated aluminium sectional doors with flush vertical grooves in Burnt Mound. The stainless tube railing becomes 50x10 mm vertical flat bars at 110 mm centres, hot-dip galvanised then powder-coated Burnt Mound.

Lapa & pool

Keep the thatch. Reed on brick is the Lowveld's own answer to heat, and it is in good condition. Re-comb it, treat it with an SABS-approved fire retardant, fit a freestanding lightning mast to SANS 10313, and open the ceiling to replace any borer-damaged poles with H4 CCA-treated or steel members. The brick lapa columns are bagged Ochre so the thatch sits on the same mass as the house. The Indian sandstone deck stays: acid-washed and sealed with a breathable impregnator, not a film sealer. The raised tiled pool edge is replaced by a flush 50 mm-overhang precast terrazzo coping with straw-coloured aggregate, and the pool is re-marbelited charcoal-green.

The signature

The 51 door: a solid oxide-red aluminium pivot gate with the numerals cut clean through, 900 mm tall, washed from behind by a warm LED reveal so that at night the fortress wall glows 51 at the street.

Five moves, priced

01One mass Salt-wash, bag and mineral-silicate limewash about 900 m² of face brick (house, both wall faces, piers, lapa columns) in Termitarium Ochre, after a trial panel.R 430 000
02Oxide lid Strip the grey boards; reclad about 180 m² of upper boxes and fascia in vertical AZ150 pre-painted steel standing seam, Burnt Mound.R 270 000
03Street gates and 51 Battened aluminium sliding gate on the existing motor, palisade infill replaced to match, laser-cut 51 pivot door with LED reveal, flush letterbox.R 195 000
04Doors and balustrade Two insulated aluminium sectional garage doors plus about 32 m of galvanised, powder-coated flat-bar balustrade replacing the stainless tube rail.R 165 000
05Lapa and dark pool Thatch re-comb, fire retardant, lightning mast, pole inspection; charcoal marbelite, terrazzo coping, sandstone deck acid-washed and impregnated.R 215 000
Budget band R 1 150 000 to R 1 550 000 total
Duration 14 weeks
Hardest risk

Bagging old face brick traps moisture. If damp-proofing has failed or salts sit in the brick, the first summer storms push efflorescence through the slurry and the monolith goes blotchy and flaky. That needs a DPC survey, salt-washing, a breathable silicate system only, and a trial panel left through one storm season before committing.

03
Qwen

Modern Kraal

QwenPaw Desktop · local agent ‘qwenpaw-local’

The minimalist’s answer: two colours and one dark blade.

monolithic sun-hardened quiet
Seven materials argue at this address — red brick, white plaster, grey cladding, dark timber, buff sandstone, turquoise water, thatch. I’m ending the argument with two. Everything masonry gets bagged and painted one warm sandstone tone, from the boundary wall to the lapa piers; every element that UV, fire or borers can eat is replaced in charcoal steel. The thatch comes off, both roofs of it, and one long raked charcoal blade takes over terrace, braai and veranda, feeding its thunderstorm-gutters into hidden jojo tanks. New gates and a laser-cut 51 pylon calm the fortress. The pool goes inky slate. Two colours, one deep-shadow room: a family fort that finally looks like itself.

Thesis One sand-coloured skin binds house, wall and lapa piers into a single calm enclosure; every shade-giving element is charcoal steel.

Palette

Escarpment Sand #D9C8A9 every bagged masonry surface: boundary wall, house body, balcony plinth, lapa piers (UV-inert silicate paint)
Coal Blade #2E2C2A steel pavilion roof, gates, fins, fascia and rainwater goods (powder-coated, hail-proof)
Ink Slate #3E4C54 pool plaster water and deep-cool accents
Oxide Ember #B0492F one warm spark: braai flue, entry pivot door, lounge cushions
Bone Paver #E8E2D4 pool deck porcelain, cool underfoot at 35C

What changes, surface by surface

Street edge · wall, gates, the 51

Render the fortress wall in Escarpment Sand with charcoal steel coping; replace scrollwork gates with flat-bar charcoal steel; inset charcoal slat panels between piers along the approach; the 51 comes off the brick as a laser-cut steel pylon, backlit at dusk.

Facade · stone, siding, garage doors

Bag and mineral-paint every masonry surface into one sand skin; repaint the grey siding the same tone so the volume reads monolithic; charcoal fascia and rainwater goods; the two dark timber-look doors become vertical-slat charcoal aluminium that never fades or feeds borers.

Lapa & pool

Both thatch roofs go; one raked charcoal steel pavilion spans veranda, dining lapa and braai, insulated IBR over a Nutec plank ceiling with box gutters feeding two hidden 5000 L jojo tanks; sand-coat the brick piers. Pool is re-marbelited in slate plaster and the buff sandstone deck lifted for 900x900 bone porcelain pavers.

The signature

The blade: one continuous charcoal-steel pavilion roof replacing both thatch forms, reading as a single dark line across the garden from the house wall to the braai chimney.

Hardest risk

New render bonding to old face brick and mixed painted plinths: if prep, key-coat and roof flashings are rushed, the first summer of thunderstorms delaminates the skin.

04
Hermes

One Wall, One Roof

Hermes Agent · profile ‘bigbrains’, deepseek-v4.1-flash

The provocateur’s answer: cut a 24 m slot in the wall.

severe cool generous
The house is fine. Its manners are wrong. Behind a two-metre brick wall it apologises, then dresses as a lodge — brown stone, timber-look garages, a thatch cone at the back. Three costumes over one modern shell. I am not adding a fourth. I am taking them off. The wall is the only real architecture on this street, so I cut it: one long slot, screened with the bricks I remove. The house behind becomes a single bone-white block under a single charcoal roof. Thatch goes. Stone goes. What stays is brick, shade, glass, water. That is the whole design. Say yes.

Thesis Stop dressing a modern house as a bushveld lodge: cut the fortress wall open, let one bone block stand under one dark roof.

Palette

Bone Lime #E7DFD1 Every rendered wall, both storeys - one mineral skin that stays cool and bleaches clean in rain.
Charcoal Oxide #2C2F2D Fascia, lapa canopy, garage slats, gate and slot rods, window frames - all metal is one colour.
Ohrigstad Brick #A07B5B The existing boundary wall and piers, kept, cleaned and repointed - the one warm surface.
Deep Pool #3E5F58 Charcoal-green waterline tile and pool interior, so the water reflects the trees, not a postcard blue.
Shade Green #55684A The clipped hedge, the tree line and all new planting - the cool third of the palette.

What changes, surface by surface

Street edge · wall, gates, the 51

The wall keeps its height and its piers. Between piers a 900mm slot opens 900mm above the pavement and runs 24m, carried on a continuous steel lintel and filled with the bricks cut out of it, set hit-and-miss. The pedestrian gate becomes one operable bay of that same screen, so you reach the front door through the slot rather than beside it; the scrollwork leaf is retired. The sliding vehicle gate is kept and recoated charcoal. '51' leaves its plaque: a recessed, bone-lined panel beside the gate, charcoal numerals, grazed by warm 2700K light.

Facade · stone, siding, garage doors

The stacked stone comes off both storeys and the grey siding comes off with it - three costumes arguing on one box. The whole volume takes a single three-coat breathable mineral render in bone, and the flat roof reduces to one 300mm charcoal fascia line. Garage doors become charcoal powder-coated aluminium slats, horizontal, borer-proof, motorised. The stainless cable rail is deleted and the balcony slab becomes a 1050mm solid parapet, so the upper floor reads as a carved loggia rather than a shelf.

Lapa & pool

The thatch goes: it is a second roof language fighting the flat roof, it cannot stop driven rain, its timber frame is borer food, and insurers load it. The brick piers stay, repointed, and a flat charcoal steel canopy lands on them - 1200mm deeper than the thatch on the weather side, continuous with the house fascia, with the braai rebuilt in masonry and its stack carried through. The pool keeps its rectangle and its sandstone: pressure-cleaned, silane-sealed, never film-sealed. A 450mm seat wall in the reclaimed bricks closes the garden edge, planted with strelitzia and plumbago. Waterline retiled charcoal-green.

The signature

A 900mm slot cut clean through 24 metres of street wall, screened with the very bricks taken out of it - the fortress becomes one long horizontal eye, and the front gate is simply the bay that opens.

Five moves, priced

01The Cut 900mm slot through 24m of boundary wall on a continuous steel lintel, hit-and-miss screen built from the bricks removed. Gates recoated; '51' recessed and lit.R 245 000
02One Skin Strip stone veneer from both storeys, repair substrate, three-coat breathable mineral render in bone. Charcoal aluminium slat garage doors; solid parapet replaces the cable balustrade.R 315 000
03The Long Roof Thatch and its timber frame out. Existing brick piers kept and repointed; flat charcoal steel canopy lands on them, 1200mm deeper on the weather side. Masonry braai stack rebuilt.R 310 000
04Cool House External charcoal louvre screens to the upper glass wall; roof insulation and whirlybirds; gutters and stormwater rebuilt for 40mm-an-hour rain. Full borer treatment, borate-sealed replacements.R 175 000

Budget band R 1.4 million to R 1.75 million total
Duration 12 weeks
Hardest risk

Cutting a 24m slot into a load-bearing boundary wall whose section nobody has opened up. If it is single-skin, the 300mm band above the slot will crack without a designed continuous lintel and new piers, and the removed bricks may be too soft or frogged to reuse as the screen. Engineer, plus a trial opening, before any saw goes in.

Before anyone swings a hammer

What all four agree you do first

None of these budgets is a quote. They are indicative 2026 allowances from four models that never measured the site. They agree on the sequence, though, and every one of them flagged the same trap: the render or the cutting is easy, and the substrate under it is unknown.

  1. A damp and salt survey of the face brick before any coating. Claude’s warning is the sharpest: if the damp-proof course has failed or salts are already in the brick, a render or bagged finish will push efflorescence through the first summer storm and the whole skin goes blotchy. A trial panel left through one storm season is cheap insurance.
  2. A structural survey of the lapa roof and its junctions with the house. Codex called this the most likely place for the budget to turn into reconstruction; the veranda strip and the lapa roof meet the house in ways nobody has opened up.
  3. If you take Hermes’s slot, engineer the lintel first. Cutting 24 m of boundary wall is the boldest move on the table and also the only one that could bring a wall down. A trial opening and a designed continuous lintel are not optional.
  4. Then measure and price. Get a quantity surveyor or architect on site with whichever direction you pick, and turn the band into a real number. Ricardo signs off money and contracts — not an agent, and not this document.

Google resolves “51 Trichard Street” to 51 Carl Trichard St, Ohrigstad, 1122 — the only number-51 Trichard Street it returns anywhere in South Africa, and the pin carries a “location not precise” flag. No town called Valkhamud was found in the Maps index. If the house is somewhere else, the designs still hold; only the climate notes would need re-checking.

On the numbers. Every rand figure in this document is an indicative allowance proposed by the design engine, not a quote, a measurement or a commitment. No supplier was contacted, nothing was ordered, nothing was paid. Treat the bands as a sizing of ambition, not a price.
